📍 Link to book — comments में।

To every parent in a NICU right now — this post is for you.

ROP is a condition that affects the developing blood vessels in the retina of premature babies. It has no visible symptoms. Babies don't show any signs of discomfort. The only way to know if your baby has it is a screening examination by a trained specialist.

Most babies who are screened have mild or no ROP. Most mild cases resolve on their own.

But when ROP is severe and goes undetected — it can cause permanent vision loss. Even blindness.

And here's the reality in India: many families are discharged from the NICU without a clear ROP referral. Not because anyone was careless. But because NICUs are stretched, parents are overwhelmed, and ROP screening can fall through the cracks.

If your baby was born before 34 weeks, or weighed less than 2000 grams at birth:

👉 Ask your neonatologist today: "Has my baby been referred for an ROP eye check?"
👉 If yes — do not miss the follow-up appointments, even if your baby seems fine.
👉 If no — ask for a referral immediately.

I'm Dr Ashish Doshi, a pediatric ophthalmologist and ROP specialist in Mumbai. I work in close coordination with NICU teams and see babies for screening and treatment.

Consultations are available in-clinic in Mumbai and via teleconsult for families anywhere in India.

If you have questions — DM me, or visit squinteyedoctor.in

I had been experiencing vision issues and tried some alternative therapies, but my condition only worsened. I finally decided to respect my eyes and consulted an ophthalmologist in my area about three months ago. While she was competent with testing, she didn't seem confident and also suggested a re-LASIK procedure, which made me doubt her expertise since I had clearly stated I wasn't interested in surgery. My sister suggested a few nearby ophthalmologists, but when I researched their reviews, the top-rated ones appeared fake while the one-star reviews were horrific. When I discovered this clinic near me on Google, I had a good feeling about it and decided to visit. Although I had to wait for an hour, it was completely worth it. Dr. Maithil took a proper medical history, and when I casually mentioned having dry eyes, he conducted a thorough, separate examination for this condition instead of immediately prescribing a lens prescription. He explained that vision numbers fluctuate with dry eyes, so he's put me on a three-week dry eye treatment before rechecking and prescribing glasses, along with eye drops for three months.

I would highly recommend Dr. Maithil. Please avoid using unscientific drops and Ayurvedic treatments on your eyes—and I say this as a yoga teacher and someone who appreciates the science of Ayurveda when applied appropriately.  Additionally, please avoid taking prescriptions from opticians and optometrists for serious eye conditions. While they are qualified for basic vision testing and lens fitting, they cannot diagnose underlying medical conditions like dry eyes, glaucoma, or retinal issues that may be causing your vision problems. Only ophthalmologists have the medical training to identify and treat eye diseases, which could be the root cause of your vision changes.

Is vision loss running in your family? It could be Inherited Retinal Dystrophy (IRD).

Inherited Retinal Dystrophy is a group of genetic eye disorders that gradually damage the retina, leading to progressive vision loss. Early symptoms often include difficulty seeing at night, poor vision in dim light, tunnel vision, light sensitivity, or blurred central vision.

Because these conditions develop slowly, they are often mistaken for common vision problems, delaying diagnosis and treatment.

Centre For Sight में विशेषज्ञ आपकी आँखों की सम्पूर्ण जाँच कर सही सलाह और उपचार प्रदान करते हैं।

Advanced Eye Technology: How Modern Diagnostics Improve Eye Care

Advanced eye technology is transforming the way eye conditions are detected, monitored, and treated. Modern diagnostic systems help eye specialists identify vision problems earlier, assess eye health with greater accuracy, and create personalized treatment plans for every patient.

From detailed retinal imaging and corneal mapping to advanced screening for glaucoma, cataracts, and refractive errors, cutting-edge technology enables safer, more precise, and more effective eye care.

Regular eye examinations combined with advanced diagnostic tools can help detect potential issues before they affect your vision, ensuring timely intervention and better long-term outcomes.

Book your comprehensive eye examination at Centre For Sight and experience the benefits of technology-driven eye care.

How Long Does LASIK Last? Understanding Long-Term Vision Correction

LASIK is designed to permanently reshape the cornea and correct vision problems such as myopia, hyperopia, and astigmatism. For most patients, the results are long-lasting, with clear vision often maintained for 10–20 years or even longer.

A common misconception is that LASIK "wears off" over time. In reality, the surgical correction remains permanent. However, natural age-related changes such as presbyopia (difficulty reading up close after 40), cataracts, or other eye conditions can affect vision later in life.

Patients with stable eye power, healthy corneas, and appropriate candidacy typically experience excellent long-term outcomes. In cases where vision changes significantly, enhancement procedures may be considered after a thorough evaluation.

If you're considering LASIK or want to learn whether you're a suitable candidate, consult our refractive surgery specialists for a comprehensive assessment.

Healthy Vision Supports Better Learning & Development in Children

Good vision plays a vital role in a child’s learning, confidence, and overall development. Clear eyesight helps children read comfortably, stay focused in class, participate actively in activities, and perform better both academically and socially.

Many vision problems in children can go unnoticed because kids may not realize their vision is different from normal. Difficulty reading, frequent eye rubbing, headaches, squinting, or poor concentration can sometimes be signs of an underlying eye condition.

Regular pediatric eye examinations can help detect vision issues early and support healthy visual development during the growing years.

Give your child the advantage of clear vision with timely eye check-ups and expert eye care.

Migraine Aura: When Visual Disturbances Need Attention

Seeing flashing lights, zigzag patterns, blind spots, or shimmering lines before a headache may be a sign of migraine aura. These temporary neurological symptoms can occur before or during a migraine and, in some cases, even without a headache.

While migraine aura is usually not dangerous, new or unusual symptoms such as sudden vision changes, speech difficulties, one-sided weakness, or symptoms lasting longer than an hour require prompt medical evaluation.

Understanding your symptoms and getting the right diagnosis can help rule out other eye or neurological conditions and ensure appropriate management.

If you experience recurring visual disturbances or unexplained vision changes, consult a specialist for a comprehensive evaluation.

featured_reviews.review_text:
On our first visit on 4 April 2026, we were informed that the consultation fee was ₹1,000 and that follow-up visits within 3 months would be charged ₹600.

When we visited again on 15 June 2026, we specifically confirmed the follow-up fee with the reception staff before meeting the doctor, and we were told that the fee would be ₹600. However, after the consultation, we were charged ₹1,000 instead.

When we questioned this discrepancy and informed the doctor that the reception staff had clearly stated ₹600, he immediately changed the explanation and claimed that the follow-up fee was valid only for 2 months, not 3 months. This directly contradicted the information that had been provided earlier.

What is even more concerning is that this confusion appears to be continuing. Patients are still being told one thing before the consultation and something different at the time of payment. They are informed that follow-up visits within 3 months cost ₹600, but later are told that the ₹600 fee is applicable only for 2 months and are charged ₹1,000 instead.

This is not a minor misunderstanding. Providing inforamtion about fee before treatment and demanding a higher fee afterward is misleading and unacceptable. Patients deserve transparent, consistent, and honest communication regarding consultation charges. Such contradictory statements seriously damage patient trust and raise concerns about the fairness of the fee policy.

Based on this experience, I would not recommend this doctor to others. The issue is not the amount charged, but the lack of transparency and the contradictory explanations given regarding the consultation fees. Patients should not be told one price before treatment and a different price afterward. Honest and consistent communication is a basic expectation, and unfortunately that standard was not met in this case.
